title: CrowdX
tagline: Real-time crowd-density monitoring that warns organisers when a zone is surging, not after it overflows.
overview: CrowdX watches two live camera feeds, detects people in every frame with YOLOv8, maps them onto a 3×3 grid of zones, and flags zones that are getting dangerously full. A trend engine estimates how fast the crowd is growing so the system can raise an early warning — over WhatsApp, a local alarm and a live dashboard — before the threshold is crossed.
problem: Crowd crushes at festivals, concerts, stations and religious gatherings build up over minutes, but the people managing them usually see the danger only once it is visible on the ground. A headcount alone isn’t enough; organisers need to know where the crowd is concentrating and how quickly it is changing.
motivation: Built during a hackathon on public safety and AI for social good. The goal was a system an event organiser could actually run with ordinary hardware: a laptop webcam and a phone used as an IP camera.
objectives: Detect and count people in real time from more than one camera
Localise density to zones instead of reporting a single number per frame
Estimate the crowd’s growth rate and project it a few seconds ahead
Alert the right people with a location link the moment risk rises
Show everything on a live dashboard
features: Two simultaneous feeds (laptop webcam + phone IP camera), each on its own processing thread
YOLOv8n person detection on every frame
3×3 zone grid per camera; each zone marked safe or unsafe against a per-zone threshold
Gaussian-blurred density heatmap overlaid on the live video
Trend engine: growth rate over a rolling window, a 10-second-ahead count projection, and STABLE / GROWING / SURGING / DECLINING labels
Two-stage alerts — surge warning and overcrowd alert — sent over Twilio WhatsApp with a Google Maps link, plus a local sound alarm
Suggested safest zone to redirect people towards
Flask + Socket.IO dashboard with MJPEG streams and JSON endpoints
Optional MongoDB logging of alerts and 10-second crowd snapshots; the app keeps running if the database is down

architecture.label: Capture

architecture.label: Zone density

architecture.label: Risk

workflow.title: Read a frame
workflow.detail: Each camera thread reads a frame and reconnects automatically after repeated read failures.

workflow.title: Find people
workflow.detail: YOLOv8n returns boxes; only the “person” class is kept.

workflow.title: Place them in zones
workflow.detail: The centre of each box is mapped to one of nine zones, giving a count per zone.

workflow.title: Score risk
workflow.detail: Zones over the per-zone threshold are marked unsafe; the total is compared with a global threshold.

workflow.title: Project the trend
workflow.detail: The trend engine computes people-per-second growth over the recent window and projects the count 10 seconds ahead.

workflow.title: Warn and broadcast
workflow.detail: On a surge or overcrowd, an alert goes out once per episode, the dashboard updates over Socket.IO, and the event is logged.

decisions.title: Zones over a single headcount
decisions.detail: Dividing each frame into a 3×3 grid lets the system say where it is dangerous and point people to the emptiest zone instead.

decisions.title: Warn on growth, not just level
decisions.detail: A projected count from the recent growth rate lets the system fire a surge warning before the overcrowd threshold is reached.

decisions.title: One thread per camera
decisions.detail: Each feed runs independently, so a dropped phone stream shows “No Signal” on its panel without stalling the other camera.

decisions.title: Database as optional
decisions.detail: MongoDB logging is wrapped so the monitoring loop keeps working if the database is unavailable — the safety path never depends on storage.

decisions.title: Alert once per episode
decisions.detail: A per-camera flag stops the system sending a message every frame; it resets when the count drops back below the threshold.

challenges.solution: The capture loop counts failed reads, releases and reopens the stream, and serves a placeholder frame in the meantime.
Alerts are latched per camera and cleared when the crowd falls back below the threshold.
A geolocation lookup provides coordinates for the Maps link, with a fixed fallback location when the lookup fails.
A simulation mode with low thresholds lets a handful of people in front of a webcam trigger the full alert pipeline.

testing: Configured to run on everyday hardware: a laptop webcam and a phone streaming as an IP camera.
Small scripts check the two external integrations in isolation: location lookup (test_location.py) and Twilio messaging (test_twilio.py).
Thresholds in config/settings.py are set for a demo-sized group; they would need calibrating per venue and camera angle.
No accuracy figures are claimed — the system has not been evaluated on a labelled crowd dataset.
limitations: Tracking is currently per-frame: each detection gets an index in that frame rather than a persistent ID, so the system counts people but does not follow individuals.
Growth rate is the slope between the first and last counts in the window, which is sensitive to single-frame detection noise.
Zone counts use a fixed grid in image space, without correcting for camera perspective.
YOLOv8n is the smallest model; dense, occluded crowds would need a larger model or a density-estimation approach.
Simulation thresholds are on by default in the current code.
improvements: Integrate DeepSORT or ByteTrack for persistent IDs and flow direction
Fit the trend with a least-squares regression and smoothing over the full window
Evaluate counts against a labelled crowd dataset and report error
Move thresholds and recipient lists into environment configuration
verification: Written from the public CrowdX repository (core/, server.py, alerts/, utils/, config/). Features listed are present in the code.
resumePoints: Computer-vision pipeline running YOLOv8 person detection across two synchronised live video feeds.
Trend engine that projects crowd count 10 seconds ahead to raise surge warnings before zones overflow.
